posts.title: Toll passes 389 as China warns lake may burst within days
body: Nepal Police put the confirmed toll at 389 dead as of a 9pm bulletin on Thursday, up from 359 at 5pm. Police also said 466 people are injured. The flood hit Timure in Rasuwa on Wednesday morning and ran down the Bhote Koshi into the Trishuli and the Narayani.

Chitwan has the most dead, 137, followed by Nawalparasi East with 87, Dhading with 33 and Gorkha with 32, Nepal Police figures reported by Review Nepal show. Health facilities in Chitwan can hold only around 50 bodies, which is slowing the process of identifying and releasing them to families.

Nepal's tourism board says 644 travellers, 517 of them foreign nationals, were reported missing in a situation update issued at noon on Thursday, up from an earlier police count of 579. India has the most missing at 178, followed by 65 Americans and 53 Ukrainians, the tourism board says. Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are down across the valley and are coming back slowly.

China's Ministry of Water Resources says a new barrier lake near the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo, close to the Nepal border, is already overflowing and holds about 2 million cubic metres of water. It expects another 3 million cubic metres to flow in over the next three days, putting the lake at high risk of breaching in that time. This is separate from the smaller lake NDRRMA found earlier on the Lhende river.

USGS first read the shaking on Wednesday as an earthquake. It later found no earthquake took place. The signal came from an ice and rock avalanche that fell into the Lhende Khola on the Tibet side, dammed the river, then broke.

Nepal's Army says more than 5,000 army and police personnel are working the flood zone, from Nuwakot to Chitwan. Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled to Bidur in Nuwakot on Thursday to see the damage.

In India, the NDRF and the Sashastra Seema Bal have rescue teams on standby in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, and the NDRF says the Gandak, which the Narayani becomes downstream, could see higher water levels. Nepal has turned down offers of search and rescue teams from India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, the Kathmandu Post reports. The government says its own army and police can handle the operation and is asking instead for cash, through a single channel into the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund.
Keep off the banks of the Bhote Koshi, the Trishuli and the Narayani until officials say it is clear.

posts.title: Damage put at Rs 200 billion, hydropower losses still being counted
body: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal said damage to roads and bridges is around Rs 200 billion. He called it preliminary information.

That figure does not include energy infrastructure. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered an immediate assessment of hydropower damage. In Rasuwa, 8 projects have been hit, 5 of them operational with a combined 236 megawatts, and 3 still under construction with a combined 342 megawatts. Nuwakot has lost access to 6 more projects, 4 operational at 123 megawatts and 2 under construction at 53 megawatts.
Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan are still being surveyed for road and building damage, so the Rs 200 billion figure is expected to rise.

The government has released Rs 1 billion to the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. The World Bank has separately offered up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance, its Nepal country director told the finance ministry. That is aid, not a damage estimate.
Insurers say claims will take weeks to settle because most of the damaged sites cannot be reached by road.

The Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund took in Rs 273.3 million in donations in its first six hours, the finance ministry says, led by a Rs 100 million gift from Gorkha Brewery. That is public donations, separate from the Rs 1 billion the government has already released for relief.

UNICEF says at least 17,000 children have been affected across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. It counts 18 schools destroyed and 20 more damaged in those three districts, wider than the 8 schools Onlinekhabar had reported damaged in Rasuwa and Nuwakot alone a day earlier. UNICEF says around 10,000 school-age children now need help such as temporary classrooms and replacement books to keep learning.

posts.title: Over 200 hydropower staff still out of contact, IPPAN says
body: The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal, IPPAN, says 215 staff from five hydropower projects have not been reached since Wednesday's flood. Worst hit is the under construction Upper Trishuli-1 project, where IPPAN counts 94 people out of contact, among them 8 Korean nationals working for the developer. At Rasuwagadhi, 51 staff are out of contact, though 3 reached higher ground on their own.

IPPAN says it has unconfirmed reports of an early rescue at one project site, but most workers there are still unreachable. Separately, a Nepal Army helicopter reached the nearby Upper Trishuli 3A project on Thursday to check on stranded staff, after two earlier landing attempts failed in bad weather. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered agencies to speed up the rescue there and get power back on.

posts.title: Australia raises its missing count to 39, pledges $5m in aid
body: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong said on Friday that 39 Australians are now unaccounted for in the flood, up from the 35 that Nepal's tourism board had listed a day earlier. She said the number could still rise as officials work through the list, and warned some of those missing may not be found.

Wong also announced A$5 million in Australian aid: 2 million to the World Food Programme, 2 million to Australian NGOs through the Australian Humanitarian Partnership, and 1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance for local recovery work. Three more Australian humanitarian specialists are being sent to join the 20 staff already in Nepal.
